description.value: This study identified functional abnormalities in emotion-regulation neural circuitry associated with developmental trajectories of behavioral and emotional dysregulation in youth using latent class growth analysis and neuroimaging.

spans.text: We aimed to identify functional abnormalities in emotion regulation (ER) neural circuitry associated with different behavioral and emotional dysregulation trajectories using Latent Class Growth Analyses (LCGA) and neuroimaging.

value: LCGA would identify distinct classes of PGBI-10M developmental trajectories in LAMS youth during the five-year course of LAMS1.

LAMS youth with more severe PGBI-10M developmental trajectory would show significantly reduced activity in prefrontal cortical regions in ER circuitry and significantly reduced prefrontal cortical-amygdala connectivity, during task performance than LAMS youth with less severe PGBI-10M trajectory and HC.

description.value: A multisite longitudinal observational study of youth with behavioral and emotional dysregulation and healthy controls, with repeated assessments and neuroimaging during an emotional n-back task.

name.value: Main effect of group on activity in right DLPFC

definition.value: significant main effect of group in right DLPFC(BA9)

value: There was a significant main effect of group in two clusters in bilateral DLPFC, including right DLPFC (F(2,241)=9.92, p<.001, corrected). LowD showed greater right DLPFC activity than HC, while HC and HighD did not differ significantly.

These findings suggest that recruiting DLPFC to a greater than normal extent during ER task performance may be necessary to help compensate for behavioral and emotional dysregulation and equate task performance with that of HC in LAMS youth.

name.value: Main effect of group on functional connectivity

definition.value: significant main effect of group on functional connectivity between bilateral amygdala and left VLPFC

spans.text: Findings from the full factorial model for functional connectivity revealed a similar pattern of a significant main effect of group on functional connectivity between bilateral amygdala and left VLPFC (BA47; F (2, 487) =11.65, p<.001, corrected, 67voxels, mni:-34, 32, -14) and between bilateral amygdala and bilateral dACC (BA 24; left: F (2, 487) =9.25, p<.001, corrected, 140voxels, mni:-2, 6, 40 right: F (2, 487) =8.44, p<.001, corrected, 171voxels, mni:4, 8, 38).

value: PPI analysis revealed a significant main effect of group on functional connectivity between the amygdala and left VLPFC. HighD showed significantly reduced positive functional connectivity than LowD between bilateral amygdala and left VLPFC, and between bilateral amygdala and two clusters in the left dACC; connectivity in HC was intermediate and did not differ significantly from either LAMS subgroup.

A combination of decreased positive/increased inverse functional coupling among amygdala, VLPFC and dACC and decreased DLPFC activity may represent a neural mechanism for impaired ER task performance that may in turn be associated with more severe behavioral and emotional dysregulation in youth.
